sections.deviations: `show()` (non-modal), not `showModal()` as the section text suggested. The picker is a popover anchored under its trigger (`.folder-picker-host` is `position: relative`, the picker is `position: absolute; top: calc(100% + 6px)`); a modal dialog lives in the top layer, where `position: absolute` resolves against the viewport, so showModal() would move it to the window's top-left corner and add a ::backdrop the design does not have. The rule's own guidance explicitly permits either: "open it with `dialog.show()` (non-modal) or `dialog.showModal()` (modal)". Moving to a real modal would need CSS anchor positioning and a visual review, which I cannot run here.

reviewNotes:
Ground truth worth keeping about the two rules I spent the most time on:

1. `no-high-complexity-react-function` counts only the component function's OWN top-level control flow — branches inside nested callbacks (useCallback bodies, event handlers, memo factories) do NOT count. Verified against DiffContents: reported cyclomatic 20 exactly matched the 19 top-level JSX/return branches + 1. The flagged floor is cyclomatic 14 / cognitive 16 (RepositoryDiffPanel at 14/16/3 was flagged). So the cheap fix is always "move a JSX branch cluster into a child component or a pure `xxxModel.ts` function", never "tidy up the callbacks".

2. `no-multi-component-file` did NOT fire on AgentPanel.tsx (13 components), GitHubPanel.tsx (3) or DiffSurface.tsx (3) but fired on all six secondary components in AppView.tsx (7). The pattern consistent with every observation is: it fires when a file has roughly 4+ components AND no component whose name matches the filename. I did not confirm this from the rule source; every new file I created has one component named after the file (at most two where the second is a tiny private helper), so nothing depends on the heuristic being exactly right.

Three things a reviewer should look at specifically:
- **useReviewDraft.ts returns fresh values on the transition render** rather than falling through with the stale ones. React discards that pass either way, so it is observationally identical, but it stops `applyReviewFileFilter` running over a large tree with the previous review's query. Slightly non-obvious; there is a comment on it and a dom test asserting the stale draft never reaches the DOM.
- **FolderPicker uses `show()` not `showModal()`** (see H1-5 deviations). This is the one place I deliberately did not follow the section text, because showModal() would break the popover's anchoring to its trigger button. Worth a visual check after `update:mac` anyway: the picker is now a `<dialog>`, and the UA sheet's `margin: auto` / `padding: 1em` are overridden in styles.css. Also check the `@starting-style` entry animation still plays — the element goes `display:none` → `display:flex` inside the layout effect, before paint, so it should, but I could not verify visually.
- **Pre-mount closure +19.6 KB** (1,361,302 → 1,380,922, limit 1,403,000). That is the price of ~90 new modules. If the ratchet is tightened after this wave, do not go below ~1,395,000 without reversing part of the split. Nothing new entered the closure — the same chunks are listed, they are each a little larger.

Carry items I did NOT touch (outside src/renderer/src or outside my sections): W3-X1 (thread `lane` through the PR path in repository.ts), W3-X2 (assert "no vendor-shiki chunk in the pre-mount closure" in check-entry-chunk.mjs — note the script ALREADY prints exactly that line, so this may be done), W3-X3 / W3-X5 (startup-probe: read `horus:palette-open-to-focus` as paletteOpenAppMs, settle `palette.emptyRows`), W3-X4 (`open(folderPath, resolved)` in repository.ts). Nothing outside src/renderer/src/** was modified by this track; no git add/commit/stash/checkout/restore was run, and neither was update:mac / dist:mac / install:mac.
